transcription.notes: Multi-subject Blitz round (mathematics, physics, chemistry, informatics) of 80 short tasks; each printed "Task N" is one problem. No points, no total and no time limit are printed. The archive has no solutions or answer file, so no answers are given and every solution is marked incomplete. The masthead is two lines ("Olympiad of Metropolises, Moscow" / "Blitz Contest, September, 5") and prints no year; the catalogue year 2016 is used for held (2016-09-05). The text layer is a Word export that drops every formula (they are embedded images), so it was used only for spelling. It spells the hex number of task 5 as 37СF and the letter list of task 69 as "А, B, …" with a Cyrillic С / А; the page shows Latin-looking letters, transcribed as Latin C and A. Program listings with braces or "<<" (task 8 C++ lines, task 26 Pascal/C two-column table, task 53 Java class) are kept as figure crops, as braces and << would be read as MDX; the alt text gives the listing. Tasks 33 and 57 (no braces) are transcribed as code blocks with the printed layout (task 57 prints "return f(f(n + 11))" unindented after a blank line; kept). The arrays of tasks 12 and 44 are set in math so their braces render. Task 73: the system of conditions is printed as an image; transcribed as LaTeX (the overline in each row spans "x_i = x_{i+1}"). Task 22: the chart is transcribed as a Markdown table with empty X and Y cells as printed; the two circuit diagrams are figure crops. Kept as printed (D-P28 and rule 1: real words, acceptable forms, or agreement errors which stay as printed on this route): task 3 "resistivity" for resistance; task 16 "characters fill them" (missing "and") and "Pixelated"; task 28 "maximum propulsive of 500 W" (missing noun); task 33 "This logic function return True" (agreement); task 36 "looses" (for loses, a real word); task 38 "one of the party guest", "when he scream" (agreement), "shouting 8 propagating", "first of all guess who was chosen"; task 51 "the word bbc 4-dictionary"; task 65 "how many of these numbers exists" (agreement); task 71 "cost 5/3 the cost"; "otherwise is stated" in the recurring instruction. Task 72 prints the speed as "3 m/c" (c for s); the unit is kept verbatim. Task 3 uses "resistivity of 20 Ohm" for a resistance; kept. Task 49 prints "M = 5.0 kg" with kg inside the formula and "g = 10m·s^-2" without a space; kept. Task 49 prints "table isμ = 0.2" with the formula glued to the word; a space is set before the math. Task 4 prints the degree sign as a superscript o ("0 oC"); kept as $^{o}$C. Task 70 prints the spring constant as k = 10 N/m with a stacked fraction; transcribed as $10\frac{N}{m}$. Task 1 prints the full stop on its own below the formula; kept. Task 62 ends without a question mark; kept. Task 32 ends without a full stop; kept.

Find out how many of these numbers exists that consist of 4 adjacent prime numbers, for example 2357 (2, 3, 5, 7) or 2345789 (2, 3, 457, 89).

problems.statement:
Bando and Bandi were given the job to paint a wall.

Bando can finish the job by himself in 3 hours, while Bandi can finish by himself in 4 hours.

They started together at 12:00.

While doing the job, they had a quarrel.

They argued for 10 minutes and during that time no one was working.

After the quarrel, Bandi abandoned the job and Bando finished painting alone.

If Bando finished painting at 14:25, for how many minutes did they work together before the quarrel started?

problems.statement: Ethanol can be produced either by direct hydration of ethylene or by the biological method using waste crops as a raw material. To obtain 370 L of ethanol (ρ = 0.8 g/cm$^3$), a bioethanol plant uses one ton (1000 kg) of wasted wheat. How many kilograms of wasted wheat are required to produce the same amount of ethanol as can be obtained from 1000 kg of ethylene? Assume, that there are no losses in the production process. (Molar mass of ethanol is 46 g/mol). Give the integer answer without units.

problems.statement:

In figure below, a thermally insulated vertical cylinder with height $L = 20$ meter and cross sectional area $A = 0.1$ m$^2$ is planted on the ground. The top part of the cylinder is open to the atmosphere with atmospheric pressure $P_{out} = 10^5$ Pa. The bottom part of the cylinder is closed. The lower half of the cylinder contains a high pressure air under a piston with mass $M_p = 300$ kg. Initially, the piston is held in place by a force so that it does not move. The data of the enclosed air is: pressure $P_1 = 3 \times 10^5$ Pa, volume $V_1 = 1$ m$^3$, temperature $T_1 = 300$ K, and heat capacity ratio $\gamma = c_p/c_v = 1.4$.

The piston is then released such that the enclosed air starts to expand and the piston moves upward. Assume in the subsequent process that the pressure and temperature of the enclosed air are uniform. What is the velocity of the piston at the top of the cylinder? The gravitational potential energy of the air can be ignored. $g = 10$ m/s$^2$. The answer should be given in m/s and rounded to the nearest integer.

problems.statement:
When the travelers in Jules Verne's novel "Les Enfants du capitaine Grant" (The Children of Captain Grant) were about to feast on a guanaco (South American lama) they had shot, they discovered that the meat had an unpleasant sour taste.

"The meat was too long kept, was it?" asked one of the travelers.

"No, but the meat had walked too much!" replied geographer Paganel and explained, "The guanaco is only good for eating when it is killed in a state of rest. If it has been long hunted, and gone over much ground before it is captured, it is no longer eatable."

For the compound that spoiled the travelers' meal, calculate the sum of the relative molecular weight and the total number of atoms in the compound molecule.

(Use integer atomic masses)
